gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Epoch's 24V 100Ah (B24100A-C) is rated 120 A continuous with a 200 A surge that lasts 60 seconds, not a one-second pulse. At 25.6 V with an assumed 90% inverter efficiency, that is about 2,765 W AC sustained and about 4,600 W for a full minute, compared with about 2,300 W AC from the 100 A BMS on the LiTime and Redodo cards. No result says either that Epoch's '11-year warranty' means free replacement only in years 1–3 and 40% off MSRP in years 4–11.
standout_why: I compared against the cited solarpoweredproject.com page, the GSIKE US 24V page (result #1 in both chats) and ryzzun.com's LiTime 24V review. Solar Powered Project covers only 12V batteries, does not normalise end-of-life thresholds and only remarks that 1 s and 5 s surges differ. The GSIKE page gives a peak rating only for its own pack (400 A for 1 s), leaves Epoch out, and lists no surge figure for LiTime, Redodo, Renogy, Power Queen or Battle Born. Ryzzun lists no surge figure and no end-of-life capacity for the LiTime 24V. None of the three gives Epoch's 60-second surge or how its warranty is structured. The LiTime product page was also cited but returned HTTP 429 on every try, so I could not check it.
decides: ChatGPT itself warned that a 100 A BMS gives about 2,560 W of DC, which falls short for a 3,000 W inverter. Measured that way, the 24V cards it showed differ in sustained power. LiTime and Redodo are 100 A. Epoch is 120 A continuous, which covers AC loads of roughly 2,300 to 2,765 W that would trip a 100 A BMS, and its 200 A surge lasts 60 s for motor or compressor starts. That supports Epoch as the pick for inverter-heavy or marine use. It does not support using Epoch with a fully loaded 3,000 W inverter: about 3,333 W of DC at 25.6 V is roughly 130 A, which is above 120 A. The case for paying $1,199 is also weaker than the headline suggests. The '11-year warranty' gives free replacement for only 3 years, against Redodo at $469.99. Epoch's own store also showed the battery as out of stock today.

findings.label: Continuous discharge
findings.note: 120 A × 25.6 V nominal = 3,072 W DC. With an assumed 90% inverter efficiency, that is about 2,765 W AC sustained. A 100 A BMS gives 2,560 W DC, or about 2,304 W AC, on the same basis.

findings.label: Peak/surge discharge
findings.note: Page wording: '200A (60 Seconds)'. 200 A × 25.6 V = 5,120 W DC, or about 4,600 W AC at an assumed 90%, for a full minute. Other surge ratings on the pages I read are 1–5 s pulses: GSIKE 400 A/1 s, and 12V LiTime 400 A/1 s and Redodo 300 A/5 s per solarpoweredproject.com.

findings.label: Cycle life
findings.note: The page says the rating applies 'at the depth of discharge, charge rate and temperature stated on the datasheet, to its end-of-life capacity', but publishes neither the DoD nor the end-of-life percentage. Epoch's resources page lists no datasheet for this model. It also says 'Over 9 years at one full cycle a day.'
